proposals.impact: Raise click-through from LinkedIn share by replacing a question-framed title that signals spiritual content Joel's ICP will skip
proposals.observation: The LinkedIn workflow shared "Is it wrong to charge for Reiki since the energy is not mine?" to Joel's profile yesterday. The title reads as a spiritual-practitioner Q&A post, which will cause Joel's ICP (ambitious 25-35 earners who don't build wealth) to scroll past without clicking. The blog writer's commit notes "new post shape copied from top-ranking healer money posts" — that template has clearly shaped the title toward a spiritual-retreat audience Joel does not serve. The post is already published so the content cannot be unpublished easily, but the title tag and meta title in the frontmatter can be changed before any further shares or indexing solidifies.
proposals.proposal: Replace the frontmatter title with one that speaks to the specific behavioural tension Joel's ICP recognises: the discomfort of pricing work that feels personal, emotional, or tied to identity — without using spiritual framing. The new title should pass the Sultanic test (only Joel could write it) and contain no banned words. The current title frames the post as a practitioner's ethics question; the replacement frames it as a money-psychology observation about pricing work you care about, which is a tension Joel's 25-35 earner audience feels directly when they undercharge for consulting, coaching, or creative work.
proposals.current_text: title: "Is it wrong to charge for Reiki since the energy is not mine?"
proposals.new_text: title: "Why people who care deeply about their work are the most likely to underprice it"

proposals.impact: Close the 15-point open-rate gap between Money Worship (37.5%) and Money Vigilance (66.7%) by replacing a weak subject line
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends — 29 percentage points below Money Vigilance (66.7%) and 15 points below Money Avoidance (52.6%). All three automations are running to subscribers who just completed the same quiz, so the audience quality is comparable. The gap is most likely a subject-line or preview-text problem on email 1, because automation step 1 sets the tone and open habit for every subsequent email. A subject line that is too generic, too clever, or too close to a cultural cliche about money worship ("You work hard, you spend hard") will kill curiosity at the inbox level before the behavioural content gets a chance.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line for Money Worship email 1 to name the specific, uncomfortable behaviour pattern rather than label the script. Joel's Money Worship subscribers have just been told their dominant pattern involves tying self-worth to earnings or spending as proof of success. The subject line should make them feel briefly, precisely seen — the way you feel when someone describes a habit you thought only you had. Keep it under 50 characters so it renders fully on mobile without a preview-text crutch.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Your money script: Money Worship
proposals.new_text: Subject: The payslip you check before you feel okay

proposals.impact: Restore the automated LinkedIn distribution that failed at 11:34 on 25 Sep, recovering reach for the Streamflation post already in queue
proposals.observation: The LinkedIn Share workflow failed at 11:34 on 25 Sep, the same day the Streamflation post was published. That post ("Streamflation is quietly draining your account, and your brain is letting it happen") is well-matched to Joel's ICP: a concrete, observable spending behaviour explained through a behavioural lens, with no spiritual framing. With 28 posts queued and the LinkedIn automation set to share 3 times a week, a silent workflow failure means the queue drains on GitHub but the shares do not land on LinkedIn. The "List Emails" workflow also failed at 12:18 the same day, which may indicate a shared API-token or secrets issue rather than two unrelated bugs. Joel should check whether the LinkedIn access token has expired before the next scheduled run fires.
proposals.proposal: Add a workflow-level failure notice that posts a Telegram alert when the LinkedIn Share job exits with a non-zero code, so Joel sees the failure within minutes rather than discovering it in Fred's next 24-hour report. This is a one-file addition to the existing linkedin-share workflow file: a final step that runs on failure and calls the same Telegram bot Fred already uses for proposal delivery, which means no new secrets are needed. Note: .github/workflows/* is in the blocked-paths list, so Joel must apply this diff manually rather than merging it through Fred's automated commit path.
